subject: Shiny app runs fine on windows, but crashes periodically when running on Ubuntu 14.04

messages.author: 9f29664a37e9d598
messages.subject: Shiny app runs fine on windows, but crashes periodically when running on Ubuntu 14.04
parts:
Hi All,

I have a shiny app that was written on a windows machine (8.1), where it runs smoothly. I have installed the app on Ubuntu 14.04 in order to use shiny-server. The app loads normally and runs normally for about 30 - 60 seconds before crashing. This happens when I run via shiny-server, or directly from RStudio.

A web browser typically gives an error like this:

The page at 10.190.60.131:3838 says:

 

DataTabIes warning: table id=DataTabIes_Table_O-Ajax

error. For more information about this error, please see

http://datatabIes.net/tn/7



When I run the app directly from RStudio, the crash corresponds to the following error (and traceback):

Error: Results must be all atomic, or all data frames
> traceback()
8: stop(list(message = "Results must be all atomic, or all data frames",
       call = NULL, cppstack = NULL))
7: .Call("httpuv_run", PACKAGE = "httpuv", timeoutMillis)
6: run(timeoutMs)
5: service(timeout)
4: serviceApp()
3: withCallingHandlers(expr, error = function(e) {
       handle <- getOption("shiny.error")
       if (is.function(handle))
           handle()
   })
2: shinyCallingHandlers(while (!.globals$stopped) {
       serviceApp()
       Sys.sleep(0.001)
   })
1: shiny::runApp()


Can anyone help me understand what is happening here? Thanks in advance...

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny app runs fine on windows, but crashes periodically when running on Ubuntu 14.04
parts:
Looks like maybe a ddply, ldply, or similar call is failing? In RStudio I'd put browser() calls right before suspicious operations and step through them a line at a time to see what line is causing it. 

It may or may not help to call options(shiny.error=traceback) or options(shiny.error=browser) to help narrow down where the error is being raised.

Aha, I get it. I didn't see any of my code in the traceback so I assumed the error was in some internal shiny function.

Thanks for pointing me in the right direction - I was able to find the problem and fix it (with a bad input to ddply, as you suspected).
